correctness.rationale: The uniform three-gap simplex relative to a designated side gives joint angle density 2/pi². The exact tangent-length identity yields r=(cos v-cos u)/(2 sin u), with support (0,1/2). Integration of the level sets gives a normalized survival integral. Its derivative evaluates by two explicit elementary primitives to the stated density. For its numerator A, the inequalities A>0 and A''<0 imply that the mode-equation function H=(1+4r²)A'-8rA satisfies H'=(1+4r²)A''-8A<0, proving uniqueness of the interior mode. Endpoint expansions and constant-density rescaling prove the sharp tails and marked limit laws; finite checker diagnostics agree but are not the proof.

value.rationale: The inradius is an intrinsic thickness measurement under the natural standard unit-side random-direction triangle model. Its complete elementary density, unique typical mode, lower endpoint logarithmic slope and upper endpoint parabolic conditional geometry are nontrivial properties not given by tabulating a moment or blindly inserting a parameter into a standard formula. They distinguish this model sharply from the commonly studied unit-circumradius or point-sampled triangles and provide reproducible exact geometric probability benchmarks.
